title: Choose the visual world for Shoot Project
question: One direction leads; my own pick and a strong alternate sit beside it. Keep it, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: The Shoot Pass
options.lineage: UAE event wristbands, gate passes and bilingual boarding passes
options.thesis: Your brief is a pass you fill in and tear off: one sentence of fields, one stub that books the shoot.
options.viewport: The whole phone screen is one sodium-yellow pass: the sentence set large as filled fields with bilingual mono labels, a perforation, and a full-width stub reading See who's free.
options.risk: If the perforation and stamp are set timidly it collapses into a yellow form; the pass must carry real structure, not a ticket sticker.

raised.raise: Every field snaps to one visible modular grid; labels and values share the same columns on every screen.
One accent, stamp blue, is reserved for live state only: the active field and the stub, never decoration.
Unset fields read as open slots of invitation, with a strict state vocabulary: open, set, needs attention.
Date and duration are set in tabular figures as the pass's time axis.
Each submitted brief is stamped with its edge code along the stub margin, the reference the client keeps.

options.label: Bilingual Wayfinding
options.lineage: UAE road and metro signage, Arabic and English set as equals
options.thesis: The brief reads like a route sign: who, what, when, where, with the emirate as the destination.
options.viewport: A green sign panel fills the top of the screen with the sentence as stacked route lines, each slot an arrowed destination, and a blue exit panel as the action.
options.risk: Road-sign green can read municipal, like a government service rather than a creative one; it is also my top-ranked candidate, so it is the more familiar choice.

options.label: Field and Capsules
options.lineage: one-colour field with floating white capsule controls
options.thesis: One colour owns the screen and every slot word floats on it as a white capsule you tap.
options.viewport: Green field, the sentence as a stack of white capsules, a detached capsule button with a green disc chevron.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on clarity, since capsules are obvious tap targets; loses on audience identification, it reads as any friendly consumer app.
options.risk: Without real photography it drifts toward a generic app template.

options.label: Hand-processed Film
options.lineage: 16mm film strips, edge codes and light leaks
options.thesis: The page as a strip of processed film.
options.viewport: A film strip with the brief in frames.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it is the photographer's material, not the client's, and with no real photos the grain becomes chrome.
options.kept: Stamped edge codes: each brief carries its reference along the stub.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.thesis: Slots as step keys you arm.
options.viewport: A row of step keys for the six slots.
options.case: Fuses poorly: wedding clients do not identify with an instrument panel.
options.kept: Empty slots as visible invitations with a strict state vocabulary.

options.label: Man-machine Grid
options.lineage: neon line diagrams on a traffic grid
options.thesis: The brief wired along a strict grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cold and abstract for people booking a wedding or a product shoot.
options.kept: One visible modular grid that every field snaps to.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A living shader behind thin type.
options.viewport: Full-screen shader with one hero word.
options.case: Fuses poorly: breaks the 200 KB budget and hides the action behind atmosphere.
options.risk: Slow on mid-range phones, unclear offer.
options.kept: One accent reserved for live state only.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: Time of day as the page's axis.
options.viewport: A building section with a travelling sunbeam.
options.case: Fuses poorly: elegant but unrelated to booking a shoot.
options.kept: Tabular figures for date and duration as a time axis.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A premium photography booking site: moody full-bleed photo, serif headline, booking widget on top.
canonCard.viewport: Dark photo hero, large serif line, the brief sentence in a rounded card with an amber button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from shootix.ae and every studio site, and it needs real photography you do not have yet.
